report.body:
Military Police in Água Clara received an anonymous tip that a man was selling
drugs from a white Volkswagen Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The operation began on the night of 4 November 2026. When officers
located the vehicle, the driver tried to flee and was caught after a short
chase. In the car, officers found a portion of a substance resembling
cocaine.

At the suspect's home, officers seized portions of marijuana, a precision scale,
drug-packaging material and money. The marijuana seized at the residence
totalled about 20 grams. A task force of Military and Civil Police then
located two other people involved at a snack bar and found 59 tablets of a
substance resembling marijuana weighing about 54 kilograms. Police also
seized about 500 grams of marijuana and a precision scale from M.V.S.S., aged
22. A further 120 grams of cocaine in 19 portions, which the first suspect
had discarded during the initial approach, was recovered from a bag.

The operation ran from the night of 4 November to 5 November 2026. Five
people were arrested in total: four in flagrante for drug trafficking and
criminal association, and one captured on an outstanding arrest warrant.
All five were placed at the disposal of the Judiciary.

The New Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in the Fifth Settlement, sentenced a woman
employed as a worker to six years of aggravated imprisonment for holding hashish
with intent to trade in Cairo's Badr police district. The court panel was
presided over by Judge Wajih Hamza Shuquair, with members Yasser Mohamed

Badr police investigation officer at a security checkpoint in the district saw
the defendant showing signs of suspicion, asked to search her belongings, she
consented, and officers found 125 brown pieces of hashish, cash and a mobile
phone.

The defendant confessed to possessing the drugs for trade, and the officer
stated the seized cash came from her dealing and the phone was used to contact
customers. A chemical laboratory report found that 30 of the 125 pieces,
weighing 9 kilograms and 350 grams, were hashish listed in the first schedule of
the anti-drug law.

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra arrested seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1 October 2026, suspected
of belonging to an organisation dedicated to drug trafficking. The
operation took place in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, where
officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish. The hashish was hidden among the legal
cargo of an articulated truck, inside large raffia sacks filled with rubber
crumb, a method used to hinder detection at police or customs checks.
Officers found seven people unloading pallets from the trailer, intending to
move the hashish into different vans for distribution. Europa Press
reported that the seven men were suspected of links to a warehouse dedicated to
storing and distributing 8,025 kg of hashish. 20minutos reported that the
hashish was hidden among material being transported legally.

The investigation began in June 2026 after a police action in Viladecans,
Barcelona, in which a van carrying about 2,400 kg of hashish was intercepted and
linked to the Cabanes warehouse. A court in Gavà had taken over the case
arising from that Viladecans seizure. ABC/EFE reported that the Cabanes
warehouse was used to store and distribute the drug. Surveillance detected
unusual activity at the warehouse, including people and vehicles coming and
going with no business activity and movements resembling loading and unloading. In early October, agents saw repeated movements of people and vans, the
arrival of an articulated truck, and several people manipulating vehicle number
plates, apparently to hinder identification. Investigators, supported by
ARRO officers from Girona, then entered the warehouse.

The 8,025 kg seized represents more than half of the roughly 14,900 kg of
hashish seized by the Mossos up to 1 October 2026. The police valued the
seized hashish at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit market. The
size of the haul made it one of the most significant operations by the Mossos
d'Esquadra and led to the activation of the Girona DIC. A firearm was found
in one of the detainees' vans during the search. The seven detainees were
brought before the Civil and Instruction Section of the Court of First Instance
of Figueres, and the investigation remains open with further arrests possible.

report.title: Driver arrested in Ceuta port with ~300 kg hashish; pretrial detention ordered
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding hashish hidden in a false bottom; a judge ordered him into pretrial detention on 15 November 2026. The haul is estimated at 100–300 kilograms pending official weighing, and the investigation continues.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. The investigation remains open, with suspicions of larger loads and of heavy vehicles hidden in spaces used to store hashish. On Sunday 15 November 2026 a judge ordered the driver into pretrial detention for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

report.body:
National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a group dedicated to drug trafficking, seizing 60 kilograms of
hashish and weapons. The investigation, run by Group I of the Narcotics
Squad of the National Police, had started months earlier and ended with five
detainees, the force said. Officers learned of a package of hashish
addressed to a man living in Palma, identified him, intercepted the package
containing 24 kilograms of hashish and arrested him on suspicion of drug
trafficking. In the first home, the main suspect's, officers found 36
kilograms of hashish, a compressed-air rifle with silencer and about 10,000
euros in cash, and arrested the man and a woman for suspected drug trafficking
and membership of a criminal group or organisation.

In the second home officers arrested a second suspect said to be in charge of
custody and transport of drugs, and found two kilograms of cocaine, several
doses, cutting substance, a pistol with 9 mm cartridges, a bow and arrows and a
hydraulic press for compressing cocaine. A further person was arrested in
connection with the case; officers suspect the drugs were distributed to third

uncovered the illegal activity of a 51-year-old local resident in July 2026. He grew narcotic-containing plants on his homestead plot, carefully tending

substation, with the KC-HIDTA task force and Taft Police Department, executed a
